cards.front: What is the multi-store model of memory?
cards.back: Atkinson & Shiffrin (1968): sensory register → short-term memory → long-term memory
7 ± 2 items

cards.front: Duration of short-term memory without rehearsal
cards.back: About 18–30 seconds (Peterson & Peterson)

cards.front: What is the working memory model?
cards.back: Baddeley & Hitch (1974): central executive, phonological loop, visuospatial sketchpad, episodic buffer
Component of working memory that holds sounds; includes the articulatory process
Long-term memory for personal events, time-stamped
Long-term memory for facts and knowledge
Long-term memory for skills and actions, e.g. riding a bike
Old learning disrupts the recall of new information
New learning disrupts the recall of old information
Forgetting because the right cues are missing (context- and state-dependent) |

cards.front: What did Loftus and Palmer (1974) find?
cards.back: Leading questions ("smashed" vs "hit") changed speed estimates: eyewitness testimony is unreliable |
Police technique to improve eyewitness recall: report everything, reinstate context, change order, change perspective |
Inability to form new long-term memories after brain damage (e.g. patient HM) |
Changing behaviour or beliefs to fit in with a group
75% of participants conformed at least once to a clearly wrong group answer on a line-length task
Conforming because you believe the group is right
Conforming to be liked or accepted by the group
Obedience to authority: 65% gave the maximum 450V "shock"
Seeing oneself as acting for an authority figure, so not responsible for one's actions

cards.front: What was the Stanford prison experiment?
cards.back: Zimbardo (1971): students given guard/prisoner roles; guards became abusive; stopped after 6 days |
A small group changes the majority's views through consistency, commitment and flexibility |
People are less likely to help when others are present (Darley & Latané) |
Each bystander feels less responsible when others are present |

cards.front: What is the fundamental attribution error?
cards.back: Overestimating personality and underestimating the situation when explaining others' behaviour |
Discomfort from holding conflicting beliefs or acting against one's beliefs (Festinger) |
A group values agreement over good decisions, ignoring alternatives |
A close two-way emotional bond between an infant and a caregiver

cards.front: What did Ainsworth's Strange Situation measure?
cards.back: Infant attachment type: secure, insecure-avoidant, insecure-resistant
Infants form one special attachment, usually with the mother, within a critical period
Infant monkeys preferred a soft cloth mother over a wire mother with food: comfort matters more than food
Young geese followed the first moving object they saw after hatching

cards.front: What are Piaget's four stages of cognitive development?
cards.back: Sensorimotor, preoperational, concrete operational, formal operational |
Knowing an object still exists when it is out of sight (sensorimotor stage) |
Understanding that quantity stays the same when appearance changes; achieved in the concrete operational stage |
Inability to see the world from another's point of view (preoperational stage) |

cards.front: What is the zone of proximal development?
cards.back: Vygotsky: the gap between what a child can do alone and with help |
Support from an adult that is reduced as the child learns |

cards.front: What is the internal working model?
cards.back: Bowlby: the first attachment acts as a template for future relationships |

cards.front: What does the sympathetic nervous system do?
cards.back: Fight or flight: increases heart rate, dilates pupils, releases adrenaline |

cards.front: What does the parasympathetic nervous system do?
cards.back: Rest and digest: slows heart rate, returns the body to normal |
A chemical that carries signals across the synapse, e.g. serotonin, dopamine |
Neurotransmitter released from the presynaptic neuron binds to receptors on the postsynaptic neuron |
Specific areas of the brain have specific functions, e.g. Broca's area for speech |
The brain's ability to change and adapt with experience or after injury |
Biological rhythms of about 24 hours, e.g. the sleep–wake cycle |

cards.front: What is the role of the hypothalamus in stress?
cards.back: Activates the HPA axis: CRH → ACTH → cortisol |
